The operators form a dual structure: the salary cap constraint acts as an external boundary condition, while the position valuation matrix and contract history trajectory define internal dynamics. The constraint enforces a global maximum on total expenditure, whereas the matrices encode local preferences and temporal trends. Failure modes include cap violations due to misalignment between valuation priorities and available resources, or overfitting historical trends to predict future outcomes without accounting for rule changes or market shocks. Dualities emerge in that high-value positions may be underpriced if they do not align with current cap mechanics, and vice versa. The system exhibits non-linear feedback loops where increasing investment in one area can reduce flexibility elsewhere, leading to cascading effects on team composition and strategic decisions.
